content_html:
Two hotel groups moved into ChatGPT this week, a day apart and at opposite ends of the market.

Radisson Hotel Group launched an app on Tuesday, built with Accenture, covering more than 1,000 hotels in over 100 countries. G6 Hospitality launched a plugin for Motel 6 on Monday, covering nearly 1,500 economy locations across the United States and Canada.

Neither will let you pay inside the chat.

Both hand travellers to the company website to complete the reservation. Radisson says in-chat booking will arrive later, alongside loyalty recognition and an AI concierge.

“AI is radically transforming how people search for and book hotel stays, and we are committed to being at the forefront of this shift,” said Gianni Di Fede, chief commercial officer at Radisson Hotel Group.

The behaviour they are chasing is established. Travellers have been planning trips inside ChatGPT for a while, and G6 cites Deloitte research showing generative AI use for travel planning has tripled in two years.

Shashank Jain, global head of technology and online revenue at G6, put the shift in blunter terms. Large language models are “fundamentally changing how people interact with technology”, he said, making discovery “more intuitive, contextual and personalized”.

Why they stop at the checkout

The restraint reads like a technical limit. It looks more like a business decision, and it matches what consumers say they will tolerate.

Accenture surveyed 25,590 people across 16 countries for its Consumer Pulse report in June. The findings split sharply by task.

Roughly three quarters would tell an agent to negotiate a deal or resolve a complaint. Just 32% would let one decide what to buy. Only 9% are open to fully autonomous purchasing.

“Payments remain the biggest barrier,” the report says.

Radisson’s announcement cites that same research, though a friendlier slice: 87% of travellers open to collaborating with an AI travel agent, and 71% expecting AI to influence at least half their hotel and airline spending within a year.

Both figures describe influence. Neither describes payment.

The real target is not OpenAI

Radisson is unusually direct about the strategy. The app, it says, forms part of the group’s “broader digital transformation and direct booking strategy”.

Direct booking means going around the online travel agencies. Hotels have paid commission to Booking.com and Expedia for two decades, and have contested the fees for most of them. China fined Trip.com $765m over hotel monopoly practices.

A ChatGPT app offers a way to reach the traveller before the agency does, then close on the hotel’s own site at the hotel’s own rate.

There is a defensive reason too. Radisson says organic and direct web traffic, the channels that historically drove its online bookings, are “giving way to new touchpoints like ChatGPT”.

That is a hotel group stating publicly that its search funnel is draining, then following the traffic to wherever it went.

The loyalty problem

The threat underneath runs deeper than distribution.

Accenture’s separate agentic commerce research found that 90% of frequent AI users in North America would abandon a previously preferred brand if their assistant suggested something better.

Radisson Rewards has more than 28 million members. Loyalty programmes rest on the assumption that habit beats comparison. An assistant that compares everything, every time, tests that assumption directly.

Appearing in the answer has become the new shelf position, and brands have spent the past year learning how to earn citations inside AI results.

Emily Weiss, Accenture’s global travel lead, named the trade-off directly. “With travel, planning is becoming easier for consumers, but more competitive for brands,” she said.

Accenture frames the choice as becoming “the agent of choice” or settling for being “the choice of agents”. Both hotel groups picked the second.

One firm on several sides

Accenture’s position here is worth stating plainly.

It published the research the release cites. It sells the MCP accelerator and AI Merchant Center that Radisson used. It designed the app experience. Ndidi Oteh, quoted in the announcement as chief executive of Accenture Song, is a named author of both reports.

Accenture is also an OpenAI Elite Partner, and says OpenAI recently named it AI Transformation Partner of the Year. None of that makes the findings wrong. It does mean the numbers come from an interested party.

What would make this real

The pieces for in-chat payment already exist. OpenAI has worked with Visa on agentic commerce payments, and Stripe’s Patrick Collison has argued that agents will reshape the commerce layer of the internet.

The hotels are not waiting for any of that. They are claiming the discovery step, which is where the agency relationship begins.

Two launches in two days, at both ends of the price range, suggests a checkbox rather than an experiment. The signal worth watching is the first major chain that lets you finish the booking without leaving the conversation.

content_html_zh:
本周，两家酒店集团入驻 ChatGPT，相隔一天，位于市场的两端。

丽笙酒店集团周二推出了一款与埃森哲合作开发的应用程序，覆盖 100 多个国家的 1,000 多家酒店。 G6 Hospitality 周一推出了 Motel 6 的插件，覆盖美国和加拿大近 1,500 个经济地点。

两者都不会让您在聊天中付款。

两者都将旅客引导至公司网站以完成预订。 丽笙酒店表示，聊天预订功能将稍后推出，此外还有忠诚度识别和人工智能礼宾服务。

丽笙酒店集团首席商务官 Gianni Di Fede 表示：“人工智能正在从根本上改变人们搜索和预订酒店住宿的方式，我们致力于走在这一转变的最前沿。”

他们所追求的行为是既定的。 旅行者在 ChatGPT 内计划旅行已经有一段时间了，G6 引用德勤的研究表明，生成式人工智能在旅行计划中的使用在两年内增加了两倍。

G6 技术和在线收入全球主管 Shashank Jain 更直白地表达了这一转变。 他说，大型语言模型正在“从根本上改变人们与技术交互的方式”，使发现“更加直观、情境化和个性化”。

为什么他们在结账处停下来

这种限制听起来像是技术限制。 它看起来更像是一个商业决策，并且符合消费者所说的他们能够容忍的程度。

埃森哲 6 月份的《消费者脉搏》报告对 16 个国家的 25,590 人进行了调查。 调查结果按任务划分差别很大。

大约四分之三的人会告诉代理人谈判交易或解决投诉。 只有 32% 的人会让自己决定买什么。 只有 9% 的企业愿意完全自主采购。

报告称：“付款仍然是最大的障碍。”

丽笙酒店的公告引用了同样的研究，不过内容更为友善：87% 的旅行者愿意与人工智能旅行社合作，71% 的旅行者预计人工智能将在一年内影响他们至少一半的酒店和航空公司支出。

这两个数字都描述了影响力。 两者都没有描述付款方式。

真正的目标不是OpenAI

雷迪森对于这一战略的态度异常直接。 该应用程序表示，该应用程序构成了该集团“更广泛的数字化转型和直接预订战略”的一部分。

直接预订就是绕过在线旅行社。 二十年来，酒店一直向 Booking.com 和 Expedia 支付佣金，并对其中大部分费用提出异议。 中国因酒店垄断行为对携程网处以 7.65 亿美元罚款。

ChatGPT 应用程序提供了一种在旅行社之前联系旅客的方法，然后按照酒店自己的价格在酒店自己的网站上关闭。

还有一个防御性的原因。 Radisson 表示，有机和直接的网络流量（历史上推动其在线预订的渠道）“正在让位于 ChatGPT 等新接触点”。

这是一家酒店集团公开表示其搜索渠道正在耗尽，然后跟踪流量到任何地方。

忠诚度问题

潜在的威胁比分发更严重。

埃森哲的独立代理商务研究发现，如果助手提出更好的建议，北美 90% 的频繁人工智能用户会放弃以前喜欢的品牌。

丽赏会拥有超过 2800 万名会员。 忠诚度计划建立在习惯胜于比较的假设之上。 每次都会比较所有内容的助手会直接测试该假设。

出现在答案中已经成为新的货架位置，品牌在过去的一年里一直在学习如何在人工智能结果中获得引用。

埃森哲全球旅行主管艾米丽·韦斯 (Emily Weiss) 直接指出了这种权衡。 “对于消费者来说，旅行计划变得越来越容易，但对于品牌来说却更具竞争力，”她说。

埃森哲将选择定义为成为“首选代理人”或满足于成为“代理人的选择”。 两家酒店集团都选择了第二个。

一家公司多面

埃森哲在此的立场值得明确说明。

它发表了新闻稿引用的研究。 它销售Radisson使用的MCP加速器和AI Merchant Center。 它设计了应用程序体验。 声明中援引埃森哲首席执行官恩迪迪·奥特 (Ndidi Oteh) 的话说，他是这两份报告的署名作者。

埃森哲也是 OpenAI 精英合作伙伴，并表示 OpenAI 最近将其评为年度人工智能转型合作伙伴。 这些都不能说明研究结果是错误的。 这确实意味着这些数字来自相关方。

是什么让这成为现实

聊天内支付的部分已经存在。 OpenAI 与 Visa 就代理商业支付进行了合作，Stripe 的 Patrick Collison 认为代理将重塑互联网的商业层。

酒店不会等待这些。 他们声称发现步骤，这是代理关系开始的地方。

两天内两次发布，在价格范围的两端，表明是一个复选框而不是一个实验。 值得关注的信号是第一家让你无需离开对话即可完成预订的大型连锁店。
